METALWORK — TERMLY EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: METALWORK
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Introduction to Metalwork, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Metalwork.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Metalwork.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Metalwork.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Metalwork.

2. When learning Safety in the workshop, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Safety in the workshop.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Safety in the workshop.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Safety in the workshop.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Safety in the workshop.

3. When learning Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.

4. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. Information and Communication Technology
   D. Input Cable Tester

5. When learning Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.

6. When learning Hand tools and bench tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Hand tools and bench tools.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Hand tools and bench tools.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Hand tools and bench tools.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Hand tools and bench tools.

7. When learning Measuring and marking out tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Measuring and marking out tools.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Measuring and marking out tools.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Measuring and marking out tools.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Measuring and marking out tools.

8. When learning Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals.

9. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Remove all guards
   B. Run with the tool
   C. Work alone with eyes closed
   D. Wear safety gear and follow instructions

10. When learning Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.

11. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   B. Overload every socket
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun

12. When learning Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 , the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .

13. When learning Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro.

14. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Monitor
   B. CPU
   C. Speaker
   D. Keyboard

15. When learning Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.

16. When learning Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3 and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Measuring and marking out tools and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
